To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of a safety network is crucial for the success of the training process; (ii) the use of weak human supervision, in the form of a human instructor, is crucial for the agent to successfully learn the task; (iii) the use of reward induction is essential for training the agent to perform the task in a safe manner; and (iv) the use of supervised imitation learning, which is based on human demonstrations, is crucial for learning the task.
we propose a new learning scheme for robotic tasks and show that it can be used to train a computer agent to perform autonomous highway steering.

a computerized agent can learn to perform complex tasks such as highway driving, using a human instructor, without access to simulator internals, and without a simulator, using only the last four elements (ii-v) of the learning scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of teaching a computerized agent a new skill, such as autonomous highway steering, using human supervision.
the problem of learning complex tasks in a computer game from weak supervision, i.e., from a few demonstrations and a reward signal.
a new approach for creating autonomous systems that are capable of learning complex human tasks using strong and weak human supervision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work demonstrates that deep learning can be used to train computerized agents to perform complex tasks, such as highway steering, in an efficient and safe manner.

our work shows the possibility of training computerized agents to perform complex human activities using a natural learning scheme, and without the need for access to the internal state of the simulated environment.
we are able to teach a computerized agent how to drive a car on a highway by providing only a few minutes of weak human supervision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a scheme for deep learning of robotic tasks using strong and weak human supervision, and show how to successfully implement it using convolutional networks.
we propose an end-to-end learning scheme for training computerized agents to perform complex robotic tasks.
we show how deep neural networks can be used for learning robotic tasks from weak supervision and how they can be used for constructing a safety module that can prevent catastrophic errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a human instructor can effectively teach a computerized agent how to perform a complex robotic task, even when the task requires a high level of human intelligence, such as driving a car.
the combination of deep learning and reinforcement learning is a powerful framework for training computerized agents to perform complex tasks using only weak supervision.
deep learning of complex human tasks can be achieved using strong human supervision, and that the use of deep convolutional neural networks is a promising approach for this goal.
